title: The pace of a sehaj path
word: The pace of a sehaj path
hook: round-ups in a savings app add up; a page a day reaches the end of the Granth too

segments.voice: Yesterday, the sehaj path: the whole Granth, read with ease, a little at a time, no deadline to fail. Your own pace. So what does a pace actually look like?
screen: `SEHAJ PATH: YOUR OWN PACE.` → `WHAT DOES A PACE LOOK LIKE?`

segments.voice: A savings app rounds every coffee up to the next dollar and tucks away the change. Nobody notices a few cents. A year later, there's a number in there that surprises people. Now the Granth. Its pages are called Angs, and the standard printing runs to Ang 1430. Yesterday's question: a page a day, how long until the end? Just under four years. Five pages a day, and you finish in under a year. Which raises the real question: is slow a problem?
screen: `ROUND-UPS ADD UP.` → `A PAGE A DAY: ABOUT FOUR YEARS.` → `FIVE A DAY: UNDER A YEAR.` → `IS SLOW A PROBLEM?`

segments.voice: The Granth's own answer comes from Sheikh Farid, a Sufi saint whose verses sit in it. In paraphrase: make patience your bow, patience your bowstring, patience your arrow, and the Creator won't let it miss. Patience isn't waiting around. It's the whole weapon. So the right pace is the one you can keep, the one that turns into a habit instead of a sprint you abandon. A page a day isn't slow. It's steady. Now a neighbor who says it in its own words. In the Buddhist Dhammapada, in Max Müller's 1881 English: "Even by the falling of water-drops a water-pot is filled." Shared ground: little by little gets there. Drops fill the pot; pages reach the end. And one honest difference. In the Dhammapada, the pot is a person filling up with good they gather by their own deeds. In Farid's lines, the archer is patient, but it's the Creator who keeps the arrow true, and a sehaj path fills a reader with the Guru's Word, not with their own. Same steady drip, different picture of where the filling comes from. Something to repeat tonight: two old traditions, far apart, both say the slow way isn't the lesser way. It's how the pot fills.
screen: `FARID: PATIENCE IS THE BOW.` · `THE PACE YOU CAN KEEP.` · `DHAMMAPADA: DROPS FILL THE POT.` · `SHARED GROUND, HONEST DIFFERENCE.` · then, large: `PAGE BY PAGE.`

segments.voice: Name your wish: a pace, a page a day, or a few lines. Name the one thing most likely to get in its way, a late night, a rushed morning. Then name your plan for it, like: if the night runs late, I'll read one line instead. Say all three quietly, and let the breath settle around the plan.
The pace of a sehaj path: how much of the Granth you read each day; a page a day takes just under four years, five a day under one. The fifteenth word of the year.
screen: `THE PACE OF A SEHAJ PATH — today's word`.

segments.voice: Your line: page by page. Drops fill the pot, and patience is the bow. Fifteen, steady.

screen: `DAY 1441 COUNTS.` → `READING THE GRANTH · 15 OF 20.` → `TOMORROW: AND ON THE VERY LAST PAGE, WHAT HAPPENS?`

howItsDone: People reading a sehaj path choose a daily amount that fits their life, a page or several, and keep a marker at their place in the Guru Granth Sahib or in a gutka or app until they reach the end.
